findings.title: updateEvent calendar fallback is dead code, passes undefined calendarId
findings.body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else-branch searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` (null/undefined/empty) which can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined on that path. Google `events.update` is then called with undefined calendarId and will fail instead of falling back to the event's destination calendar or primary.

findings.title: deleteEvent calendar fallback is dead code, passes undefined calendarId
findings.body: In deleteEvent calendarId is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback compares against that same falsy value and never matches, so calendarId is undefined and the code relies on `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` only by accident. For any truthy-but-mismatched case and for future edits this logic cannot select the correct destination calendar and deletes from the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Meet fallback dereferences possibly undefined destination calendar
findings.body: Code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. If destinationCalendar is undefined, null, or empty array, the destructured value is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws TypeError, crashing event creation for bookings without a destination calendar. Must use optional chaining with fallback.

findings.title: Collective team calendars silently dropped when organizer has no calendar
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null` and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` for COLLECTIVE. When both organizer sources are missing the value is null, optional chaining skips the push, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars for the other hosts are lost and only one/no calendar event is created.

findings.title: Non-Google services ignore credentialId and always use first calendar
findings.body: Google createEvent was updated to select `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` but Office365, Lark (line 128: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), and BaseCalendarService still only use the first array entry. EventManager loops per-destination and passes the credential, so the second collective host's event is still created in the first host's calendar for all non-Google integrations.

findings.title: Breaking Calendar interface and webhook payload change
findings.body: Changing `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and `createEvent(event)` to `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` breaks all external Calendar implementations and changes webhook payloads from `destinationCalendar: null` to `[]` (as updated in webhook.e2e.ts). Consumers expecting null or single object will break. The new parameter should be optional and payload compatibility should be preserved or documented as breaking.
